id: coffee
general_english: Coffee is a beverage brewed from roasted, ground coffee beans. Dark-colored and bitter, coffee has a stimulating effect on humans due to its caffeine content; however decaffeinated coffee is also commercially available. There are also various coffee substitutes.
mini_english: Coffee is a drink that people make from beans (small brown seeds of a plant) that they burn and break into small pieces.

id: It is dark and bitter, and it makes people more awake because of the caffeine (a thing in coffee that makes you more awake).
You can also buy coffee without caffeine in a shop, and there are other things people use instead of coffee.
wall
general_english: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications in China. They were built across the historical northern borders of ancient Chinese states and Imperial China as protection against various nomadic groups from the Eurasian Steppe. The first walls date to the 7th century BC; these were joined together in the Qin dynasty. Successive dynasties expanded the wall system; the best-known sections were built by the Ming dynasty (1368-1644).
mini_english: The Great Wall of China (a very long wall in the north of China) is many old walls in one line.

id: They were built on the north side of old Chinese kingdoms (a country that a king rules) to stop people who came on horses from the north.
The first walls were made in the 7th century BC (before Christ), and later the Qin dynasty (the time when China was first one country) joined them together.
After that, every dynasty made the wall bigger. The parts we know best today were made by the Ming dynasty (1368-1644).
curie
general_english: Maria Salomea Sklodowska Curie, better known as Marie Curie, was a Polish and naturalised-French physicist and chemist. She shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with her husband, Pierre Curie, "for their joint researches on the radioactivity phenomena discovered by Professor Henri Becquerel". She won the 1911 Nobel Prize in Chemistry "[for] the discovery of the elements radium and polonium, by the isolation of radium and the study of the nature and compounds of this remarkable element".
mini_english: Marie Curie (a woman from Poland who later became French) was a scientist (a person who studies how the world works) who studied physics (the study of how things move) and chemistry (the study of what things are made of).

id: In 1903 she got the Nobel Prize (a big prize for science) in physics with her husband Pierre Curie. The reason was their work together on radioactivity (when the atoms of a thing break and give out energy).
In 1911 she got the Nobel Prize in chemistry, because she found 2 new elements (a kind of matter): radium and polonium.
bicycle
general_english: A bicycle, also called a pedal cycle, bike, push-bike or cycle, is a human-powered or motor-assisted, pedal-driven, single-track vehicle, with two wheels attached to a frame, one behind the other. A bicycle rider is called a cyclist or bicyclist.
mini_english: A bicycle (a vehicle with 2 wheels that you go forward by pushing the pedals with your feet) is also called a bike.

id: It can go by the power of your legs, or with a small motor.
The 2 wheels are on a frame (the strong part that holds them), one behind the other.
A person who rides a bicycle is called a cyclist.
antikythera
general_english: The Antikythera mechanism is an ancient Greek hand-powered orrery built in the 2nd century BC and discovered in 1901. It is the oldest known example of an analogue computer. It could be used to predict astronomical positions and eclipses decades in advance. It could also be used to track the four-year cycle of athletic games similar to an olympiad, the cycle of the ancient Olympic Games.
mini_english: The Antikythera mechanism (a very old machine from Greece) is a machine that shows the movement of the sky. People made it by hand in the 2nd century BC and people found it again in 1901.

id: It is the oldest computer we know that works like a computer today, but with wheels and gears (round things that go around and around).
With it, people could say where the stars and the sun would be in the sky many years later.
It could also show the 4-year cycle of the Olympic Games (a big sport event in Greece).
dog
general_english: A Dog was lying in a Manger on the hay which had been put there for the cattle, and when they came and tried to eat, he growled and snapped at them and wouldn't let them get at their food. "What a selfish beast," said one of them to his companions; "he can't eat himself and yet he won't let those eat who can."
mini_english: A dog was lying on the food of the cows (big animals that people keep to get milk and meat).

id: When the cows came and wanted to eat, the dog made a low sound and showed his teeth at them, and he did not let them eat.
What a selfish animal, said one cow to the other cows. "He cannot eat it himself, but he will not let the ones who can eat it eat."
